findings.rationale: The plan does not put pending_after on /v1/stream. §2.5 (poll-only harness) attaches pending_after/pending_capped to GET /v1/messages only; §2.2 gives SSE clients the `backlog` event instead, and §2.3 is about cursor/delivered_at semantics. An SSE client that wants the count has it in `backlog.pending`; a response-body field on a text/event-stream endpoint has no consumer. Parity is by event vs field, not by duplicating the field.

fetchInboxIdsAfter (store.ts) copies fetchInboxSince's WHERE clause verbatim: `to_handle NOT LIKE '@mailbox:%'` is a constant pattern, to_handle/team/since/instance are all positional bindings, and with a pollerInstance the directClause excludes rows whose meta.sender_instance equals the poller — the same self-exclusion the page applies. The route passes the same `pollerInstance` (undefined when the header is absent, exactly as for the page), so count and page share one predicate by construction; ownsNamespace is applied on top in the route just as for the page. T7/T7b exercise the count against the page. No injection surface and no parity gap.
